meta_description: Distance Reiki for people between two countries — sessions from London, Dubai or a plane, time zones, and what a founder between Nice and London found.
body:
If you live between two places, a session doesn't have to stop when you leave one of them. Distance Reiki is the same 45 minutes, the same sequence and the same attention, given from Cannes while you lie down in a flat in London, a hotel in Dubai, or a reclined seat somewhere over the Alps. We agree a time in your zone; you lie down; I message when it's done. The rhythm of sessions carries on regardless of the geography.

A lot of my clients live this way — a founder with a company in London and a house in Villefranche, a family that winters on the Riviera and summers in Scandinavia. This is how it works for them.

## The problem with living in two places

Rest needs continuity. If you've built a month of sessions and then you're away for three weeks, the body loses the thread, and the first session back is partly a restart. For people who are always partly elsewhere, that means never quite getting past the beginning.

Distance sessions solve exactly that. Session three can be in London on a Wednesday evening; session four back in Cannes the following week. The body doesn't notice the difference in the way you'd expect.

## Time zones

I work from Cannes, on French time. London is an hour behind — easy. Dubai is two or three ahead, depending on the season — an evening session there is an afternoon one here. New York is six behind — a morning session there is an early evening one here. All workable. I'd rather do a session at 10 pm my time than have you miss it.

## What you do from London

Find a quiet hour. Bed or sofa. Phone on silent. Lie down at the agreed time, fully clothed, and do nothing in particular — rest, doze, think, whichever happens. At the end my message arrives. We exchange a line or two about what you noticed, if you want to.

## What I do from Cannes

I give the full session on a proxy — a physical stand-in for your body — in the same sequence I'd use with you on the table. Head, throat, chest, stomach, lower body, feet. Same pace, same attention. There's a longer explanation of the proxy method in [how distance Reiki works](/journal/distance-reiki-how-it-works/); the short version is that my hands have somewhere to be and you receive the attention.

## What a founder between Nice and London found

He'd done three sessions in Cannes over a fortnight and then had to be in London for a month. We did the fourth and fifth as distance sessions, Wednesday evenings, him in a flat in Marylebone and me here. He told me afterwards he'd expected them to be a lesser version. What he noticed was that they were quieter — no one in the room, no journey to get there — and that the sleep afterwards was the same. He kept the Wednesday slot when he came back.

## On the plane

Yes, genuinely. A long-haul flight is an hour you can't do anything with anyway. Reclined seat, eye mask, agreed time — a session mid-flight is one of the more useful things I do for people who fly a lot, and it changes the arrival. If you want this, tell me your flight time and I'll work out the overlap.

Reiki is complementary in any form; a distance session doesn't replace medical or psychological care, and nothing about it changes that.

## FAQ

**Can I have Reiki sessions when I'm travelling?**
Yes. Distance sessions continue the rhythm from anywhere — London, Dubai, a plane. We agree a time in your zone, you lie down, I give the session from Cannes.

**How do time zones work for distance Reiki?**
I work on French time and adapt. London is an hour behind, Dubai two or three ahead, New York six behind. We find a slot that's quiet at your end.

**Is distance Reiki as effective as in person when travelling?**
Clients who've done both report the same sleep and the same settling. Some find the distance version quieter, since there's no one in the room and no journey.

## If you're between two places

Message me on WhatsApp with where you'll be and when. A distance session is €180, the same as in person, and it fits into any package — sessions don't have to all be in the same country.

title: Reiki for Entrepreneurs: One Hour Where Nothing Is Asked of You
meta_title: Reiki for Entrepreneurs: One Hour Nothing Is Asked
meta_description: Reiki for entrepreneurs — why the person who holds everything can't rest, and what one hour with nothing asked gives that a holiday doesn't. Cannes.
body:
I spent ten years in corporate coaching and investing before I did this. I know what it costs to be the person a company runs through — the one who is never fully off, whose phone is a nervous system, whose holidays are working weeks with a better view. So when I say Reiki for entrepreneurs is one hour where nothing is asked of you, I mean it as an entrepreneur would hear it: not "relaxing," but a genuine, measurable absence of demand, which is the thing you haven't had in years and the thing your body is quietly falling apart without.

This is what I see in the founders and investors who come to me in Cannes, and what changes.

## Why founders can't rest

Rest requires the body to believe nothing needs it. A founder's body has learned, over years, that something always does. The alert system doesn't switch off at 7 pm; it doesn't switch off in Mauritius. It just runs quieter, scanning. Sleep is light. Weekends are shorter than they look. The mind can decide to take time off; the nervous system doesn't take instructions from the mind.

This is why so many founders describe holidays that didn't work. The scenery changed. The state didn't.

## What a session actually is, for you

Forty-five minutes on your back, fully clothed, at your home or my space in Cannes. Hands resting lightly on the body in a set sequence. No conversation. No instruction to relax, no breathing to do correctly, no visualising. The phone is in another room, and — this is the part that matters — nobody in the room wants anything from you. Not even me. I'm not asking you to feel something.

Most founders spend the first ten minutes drafting an email in their head. Then, without deciding to, they stop. The jaw lets go. The shoulders drop. The breath gets longer. That drop is the body receiving the signal it's been waiting years for: *nothing is needed right now.*

## What one investor found

He ran a fund from Cap d'Antibes, was sceptical to the point of amusement, and booked one session because his wife had. He told me afterwards he'd spent twenty minutes composing a term sheet in his head and couldn't account for the next twenty-five. He slept nine hours that night, which he said hadn't happened since before the fund. He came back weekly for a month. He still doesn't believe in energy work, and I've never asked him to.

## What changes over four sessions

The first session is a glimpse. By the third or fourth, spaced a week apart, the body starts to expect the drop — it happens faster, goes deeper, and starts to be available outside the session. Founders describe it in practical terms: sleeping through, snapping less, a meeting where they noticed they weren't braced. That's The Renewal: four sessions over three to five weeks. It's the shape I suggest for most people in your position, and I'll tell you if one is enough.

## What I won't do

Coach you. I did that for a decade and this is a different thing — you're not here to be improved. Sell you a package before a session. Tell you it fixes anything a doctor should see: Reiki is complementary, and if the sleeplessness or the chest tightness needs a doctor first, I'll say so.

## What "off" costs you

Founders sometimes tell me they can't afford an hour off. I'd turn that round: the hour is the only thing that makes the other twelve worth anything. A decision made from alert is narrower and more defensive than one made from a body that's stood down. A conversation with a co-founder from alert is an argument. The hour isn't a break from the work. It's the condition the work is better in.

## FAQ

**Why do entrepreneurs struggle to rest even on holiday?**
Because the nervous system has learned that something always needs them. It doesn't take instructions from the mind; it needs a bodily experience of nothing being required, repeated until it believes it.

**What does a Reiki session do for a founder?**
It gives 45 minutes in which nothing is asked — no demand, no performance, no one wanting anything. The body reads that as safety and stands down, often for the first time in years.

**How many sessions should an entrepreneur start with?**
One, to find out. Four over a month if the first one shows you what you've been missing. I never suggest a package before a first session.

## If you're the one everything runs through

Message me on WhatsApp — one line about what isn't working. Single session €180, The Renewal €640, at your home, your office after hours, or my space in Cannes.

title: Is Reiki Safe? Side Effects, Contraindications, and What I Won't Do
meta_title: Is Reiki Safe? Side Effects and Contraindications
meta_description: Is Reiki safe? Yes — what people feel afterwards, who should check with a doctor first, pregnancy and children, and the one thing I won't do.
body:
Reiki is safe. Nothing enters the body, nothing is applied, nothing is manipulated; hands rest lightly on or above a fully clothed body for 45 minutes. There are no known contraindications in the medical sense, and the things people feel afterwards — tiredness, emotion, thirst — are what a nervous system does when it stands down, not side effects. The only real risk associated with Reiki is a practitioner who tells you to stop seeing your doctor. I'm not one of them.

That's the short answer. Because "is reiki safe" is one of the most-searched questions in France, here's the long one, honestly.

## What you may feel afterwards

**Tired.** Most common. You've been in deep rest and the body wants to continue. Sleep that night is usually good.

**Emotional.** Some people cry during or after, without a story attached. It's release, not distress, and it's gone by the next day.

**Thirsty, occasionally a mild headache.** The same as after a massage. Water.

**Very little.** Some people feel nothing much during and notice the difference in sleep or mood the next day.

None of this requires managing. It's what the body does when it's been allowed to stop.

## Who should tell their doctor first

Not because Reiki is known to interfere with anything — it isn't — but because your doctor should know what's around your care:

- **Pregnancy.** Reiki is widely used in pregnancy and is gentle, but tell your midwife or obstetrician. I adjust position and I don't work on the abdomen in the first trimester.
- **Pacemaker or implanted device.** No known interaction, but say so.
- **Cancer treatment.** Many oncology units allow Reiki for relaxation. Tell your team, and keep every appointment.
- **Psychiatric conditions.** Deep relaxation can bring feelings up. If you're under care, your clinician should know.
- **Children.** Always alongside their paediatrician; sessions are shorter and a parent stays.

I'll ask about all of this before we book. If something needs a doctor first, I'll tell you.

## What Reiki doesn't do

It doesn't treat, cure or diagnose. It doesn't replace medication, therapy, or a single appointment. It doesn't "detox" anything or "boost" anything — if a practitioner uses those words, they're selling. What it does is produce deep rest and settle the nervous system, which is useful alongside almost any care and dangerous alongside none.

## The one thing I won't do

Advise you to stop treatment, delay a diagnosis, or use a session instead of a doctor. That is where Reiki becomes unsafe — not in the room, but in the advice around it. Reiki is complementary. It sits next to medical care; it is not care.

## Why it's safe to try

If nothing happens, you've rested for 45 minutes in the middle of a day in Cannes. If something happens, you'll know, and you can decide from there. There is no dose, no risk of too much, and no version of a session that leaves you worse than you arrived.

## What I do if something comes up

Occasionally a session brings something up — a memory, a wave of feeling, tears that arrive without a reason attached. I don't interpret it and I don't push. I stay where I am, keep my hands where they are, and let it pass, which it does. Afterwards, if you want to talk, I listen; if you don't, we don't. And if what came up is something a therapist should hear, I'll say so — gently, and once.

## FAQ

**Is Reiki safe?**
Yes. No physical risk, no known contraindications, nothing applied. The only risk is using it instead of a doctor, which I never advise.

**Does Reiki have side effects?**
Not in the medical sense. Tiredness, emotion or thirst for a few hours afterwards is what a nervous system does when it rests deeply. It passes.

**Is Reiki safe during pregnancy?**
It's widely used and gentle. Tell your midwife or obstetrician, and I'll adjust position and avoid the abdomen early on.

## If you'd like to try once

One session, €180, at your home or my space in Cannes. Message me on WhatsApp and tell me anything medical I should know — I'll tell you honestly if a doctor should come first.

title: Reiki and Medical Treatment: How They Work Alongside Each Other
meta_title: Reiki and Medical Treatment: Working Alongside
meta_description: Reiki and medical treatment aren't rivals. How sessions sit alongside your doctor, what to tell your care team, and the line I never cross.
body:
Reiki and medical treatment are not alternatives to each other. Medicine treats the condition; Reiki settles the person going through it. The right order is always doctor first, sessions alongside — and any practitioner who reverses that order, or blurs it, is the one to walk away from.

I say this on my homepage, in every FAQ, and now here at length, because it's the question underneath most of the others people bring me in Cannes: *can I do this and still do what my doctor says?* Yes. That's the only way I'll do it.

## What Reiki does that medicine doesn't

Medicine works on the disease. It doesn't, mostly, work on the state of the person who has it — the fear before a scan, the sleeplessness of a long treatment, the body braced for months against pain or news. That state isn't nothing. It affects how you sleep, eat, tolerate treatment, and feel between appointments.

A session works on exactly that. Forty-five minutes of deep rest with nothing asked of you. Hands resting lightly on the body. The nervous system stands down. Nothing about the disease changes. Quite a lot about the day does.

## What medicine does that Reiki can't

Diagnose. Treat. Cure. Prescribe. Monitor. Decide. None of that is mine and I don't pretend any of it is. If you tell me about a symptom, I'll ask if a doctor has seen it, and if not, that's your next step before we book anything.

## Where sessions fit

- **During recovery** — after surgery, after an illness, in the long tail after COVID or flu — for the tension and the sleep, alongside whatever the doctor prescribed.
- **During long treatment** — some oncology units in the UK and US allow Reiki on wards for exactly this reason: calm patients do better and it costs nothing in risk. Always with the care team's knowledge.
- **While living with a diagnosis** — thyroid, hormonal, cardiovascular, chronic pain — for the state around the condition, with every appointment kept.
- **When waiting** — for results, for a decision, for a date. The waiting is often the hardest part and it's entirely in Reiki's territory.

## What to tell your doctor

"I'm having Reiki sessions for relaxation alongside your treatment." That's the sentence. Most doctors will say fine. A few will be sceptical about whether it does anything, which is fair. None should object to a patient resting more, and if one does, I'd want to know why.

## The line

I don't advise on medication. I don't suggest delaying anything. I don't say "try this first." If you're on treatment, you stay on it. If you're due a test, you take it. If your doctor and I ever seem to disagree, your doctor wins, and I'll be the first to say so.

There's a longer piece on whether Reiki is dangerous — the answer is no, with one exception, and the exception is exactly this line.

## A practical example

A client in Antibes was six weeks into a long course of treatment, sleeping badly, braced against every appointment. Her care team knew she was having sessions; one of her nurses had suggested it. We did one a week at her home, on the days between hospital visits. Nothing about her treatment changed. What changed, she said, was the days in between — she slept, she ate, she stopped dreading the drive to Nice. That is the whole of what I offer alongside medicine: the days in between, made livable.

## FAQ

**Can I have Reiki while on medical treatment?**
Yes. Sessions sit alongside treatment for rest and settling; they don't interact with medication and don't replace any appointment. Tell your doctor you're doing it.

**Does Reiki interfere with medication?**
No. Nothing enters the body and nothing is applied. There's no known interaction with any medication or device.

**Should I tell my doctor I'm having Reiki?**
Yes — "for relaxation alongside your treatment." Your care team should know what surrounds your care, and I'll always ask if they do.

## If you're going through something

Message me on WhatsApp and tell me what your doctors are doing. I'll tell you honestly where a session fits — and it will be alongside them, not instead.

title: How Much Does Reiki Cost on the French Riviera — and Why

body:

A French practitioner working from a cabinet in Nice typically charges €50–€80. Platforms like Treatwell and Airbnb Experiences list sessions from €85 to €140. |---|---|---|

| Platform booking (Treatwell, Airbnb Experiences) | €85–€140 | Variable quality, often a studio or spa |
| English-speaking, mobile, in-home | €150–€220 | They come to you; discretion; often distance too |
| Retreat add-on / hotel spa | €200+ | Wrapped into a larger package |

A 45-minute session — at your home, villa, hotel room, yacht, or my space in Cannes. Travel within Cannes, Le Cannet, Mougins, Antibes, Cap d'Antibes, Juan-les-Pins and Nice is included. Monaco and Saint-Tropez are on request with a small travel addition agreed in advance.

A short WhatsApp exchange before, and a short one after. No forms. English, Russian or Ukrainian. Complete discretion — I don't discuss who I see. Same-day and next-day slots are often possible.

Because I come to you, in your language, and I don't run a waiting room. A cabinet practitioner sees eight people a day in one room; I see two or three in a day across the coast, and each one gets the whole hour and the drive. That's the arithmetic. If you'd rather come to me in Cannes and pay less, ask — it's a fair conversation.

Packages are paid before the first session. Rescheduling is free with 24 hours' notice. I'll never suggest a package before you've had a session.

## Distance

€180, the same as in person. Same 45 minutes, same sequence, from Cannes to wherever you are. It fits inside any package — sessions don't have to all be in the same country.

## Children

Shorter — fifteen to twenty-five minutes — and priced accordingly. Ask on WhatsApp; it depends on age.

## How to pay

Card via a secure link, bank transfer, or cash. Whichever is easiest.

Whether the practitioner is trained in a lineage, whether they'll come to you, whether they'll tell you to see a doctor when you should. €30–€80 at a French cabinet, €85–€140 on booking platforms, €150–€220 for English-speaking, in-home practitioners. Mine is €180 for 45 minutes with travel included on the central Riviera.

Generally no. Some mutuelles include a small annual allowance for "médecines douces"; it's worth checking yours, but don't count on it.

If you need three or more sessions, yes — the per-session price drops and the rhythm matters more than the saving. If you need one, buy one.

title: Reiki for Grief: When You've Lost Someone Far From Home
meta_title: Reiki for Grief When You've Lost Someone Far Away
meta_description: Reiki for grief when the loss happened in another country — why the body holds it differently abroad, and what a session gives that talking doesn't.
body:
Grief abroad has a particular shape. The phone call comes at the wrong hour. You fly, or you can't. The funeral is in a language and a place that used to be yours, and then you come back to a life where nobody knew the person and the day carries on as if nothing happened. The body holds all of that — the shock, the flight, the return — and it holds it alone, because the people who'd normally hold it with you are in another time zone.

I won't tell you Reiki helps you grieve. Grief isn't a problem to be helped. What I can tell you is that grief lives in the body as much as the mind — the chest that won't fully open, the sleep that doesn't come, the exhaustion that has nothing to do with effort — and that a session works on exactly that layer, quietly, without asking you to talk about anything.

## What the body does with loss

It braces. Against the next call, the next wave, the moment in the supermarket when a song comes on. Grieving people describe a tightness across the chest and throat, a stomach that's clenched for weeks, sleep that's either impossible or the only thing they want. This is the nervous system in alert, the same as after any shock — except that grief keeps re-shocking, so the alert doesn't end.

Talking helps the mind make sense of it. The body doesn't make sense of things. It needs something else.

## What a session is, for grief

Forty-five minutes lying down, fully clothed, at your home or my space in Cannes. Hands resting lightly on the body — I stay longer at the chest and the throat, where grief tends to sit. No conversation, unless you want it. Nothing to process, nothing to say, no one asking how you're doing.

What people describe is the chest opening, sometimes with tears that come without a thought attached, and then a heaviness that turns into the first real rest in weeks. One thing I hear often: "I hadn't cried yet." The body sometimes waits for a place safe enough.

## Why it's different from talking

There's a limit to how much a grieving person wants to say, and a limit to how much saying it does. A session asks nothing. It's an hour where the loss is held without being discussed — where you can be exactly as broken as you are, without managing anyone else's reaction to it. For people who've been holding it together for a partner, for children, for colleagues, that hour is often the first time they've stopped.

## Far from home, specifically

If you flew back for the funeral and returned to the Riviera, you've done grief in two places, and the second place doesn't know. Neighbours in Antibes don't know. The school run doesn't know. A session at home, in the place that doesn't know, is a way of letting the loss exist here too — of not having to leave it in the other country.

## Over time

One session is a place to stop. Four over a month — The Renewal — is what I'd suggest for the weeks after a loss, when the first shock has passed and the long part begins. Not to move you through it faster. To give the body somewhere to put it down, regularly, so it isn't carrying it every hour.

Grief that turns into something else — that doesn't lift at all after months, that stops you functioning, that brings thoughts of not wanting to be here — needs a doctor or a therapist, and I'll say so plainly if I hear it. Reiki is complementary. It sits alongside that care and never in place of it.

## FAQ

**Can Reiki help with grief?**
It works on the body's side of grief — the braced chest, the clenched stomach, the sleep that won't come — without asking you to talk. It doesn't shorten grief; it gives the body somewhere to rest inside it.

**What does a Reiki session for grief feel like?**
Often the chest opens, sometimes with tears that arrive on their own, then deep rest. Many people say it's the first time they've stopped holding it together.

**When should grief be seen by a doctor?**
If it doesn't lift at all after months, stops you functioning, or brings thoughts of not wanting to be here. Sessions sit alongside that care, never instead.

## If you've lost someone

Message me on WhatsApp — you don't have to explain. One session, €180, or four over a month, €640, at your home. I'll come to wherever the loss is.

title: Can't Switch Off From Work? Your Nervous System Is Still at the Desk
meta_title: Can't Switch Off From Work? Body Still at the Desk
meta_description: Can't switch off from work even at home? It's not discipline — your nervous system is still in work mode. What that is and what settles it.
body:
You close the laptop and the work doesn't stop. It follows you to the terrace, into dinner, into bed at 1 am where you're composing a reply to an email that hasn't arrived yet. You've tried the advice — no phone after nine, a hard stop at seven, a walk by the sea in Antibes — and the body comes with you, still at the desk.

This isn't a discipline problem. Discipline is a mind thing, and the mind has already left work. It's the nervous system that hasn't. It's still running the posture of a working day — shoulders up, breath short, attention scanning — because nobody told it the day was over in a language it understands.

## The setting, not the schedule

The nervous system doesn't read clocks. It reads bodily signals: stillness or movement, tension or ease, demand or no demand. A day of calls and decisions puts it in a setting — alert, ready, braced. That setting doesn't reset when you close the laptop, because closing a laptop is not a bodily signal. It resets when the body gets enough signals of the opposite: stillness, warmth, nothing needed.

Most people never give it those signals. They go from desk to dinner to screen to bed, and every one of those has demand in it. So the setting stays.

## Why holidays don't fix it

A holiday changes the scenery, not the setting. People arrive in Cannes for two weeks and spend the first four days exactly as braced as they were in the office, in nicer light. The body can be on a sunlounger and still at the desk. By day five it starts to let go — and then it's time to think about going back.

## What "switching off" feels like when it actually happens

Most people have forgotten. It feels like the shoulders being lower than you knew they could be. Like the breath going all the way down. Like an hour going by without checking. Like being tired in a soft way rather than a wired way. It's a physical state, and if you can't remember the last time you were in it, that's the diagnosis — not of anything medical, just of a system that's been on for too long.

## A session as the signal

This is what a Reiki session is, for someone who can't switch off. Forty-five minutes of the exact signals the nervous system needs: lying still, fully clothed, hands resting lightly on the body, nothing asked. Not to relax, not to breathe correctly, not to stop thinking. The thinking usually stops on its own around minute ten, when the body gets enough evidence that nothing is needed and drops.

Founders and executives I work with describe it in practical terms. "I didn't think about work for forty minutes and I don't know where they went." "I slept through for the first time in a month." "I noticed on Thursday that I wasn't braced in the meeting."

One session shows the body what off feels like. If it's been on for years, four over a month — The Renewal — is where off starts to become available at 7 pm as well.

## What it won't do

Fix a workload that's genuinely impossible. Replace a doctor if the sleeplessness has become something a doctor should see. Reiki is complementary — alongside care, not instead of it. What it does is remind a body that has forgotten how to stop that stopping is still possible.

## FAQ

**Why can't I switch off from work even at home?**
Because closing the laptop isn't a signal the nervous system understands. It stays in work mode until it gets bodily signals of safety — stillness, ease, no demand — for long enough to believe them.

**How do I stop thinking about work at night?**
Not by deciding to. By giving the body a real experience of off — deep rest with nothing asked — so the setting changes. One session usually shows what that feels like.

**Is not being able to switch off a sign of burnout?**
It's one of the earliest. If rest doesn't restore you and the mind won't leave work, the nervous system has been on too long. It's recoverable, and the first step is one hour of genuine off.

## If your body is still at the desk

One session, €180, at your home after hours or my space in Cannes. Message me on WhatsApp and tell me when your day actually ends — I'll book just after it.

title: Reiki for Kids Adjusting to a New School and Language
meta_title: Reiki for Kids Adjusting to a New School and Language
meta_description: Reiki for kids adjusting to a new school and language — what adjustment stress looks like at 6 pm, a short gentle format, alongside the paediatrician.
keyword: reiki for kids adjusting to new school
body:
A child starting a new school in a new language is doing something most adults would find exhausting: listening all day to words they half understand, reading a room they don't know the rules of, and being cheerful about it. They hold it together until 4 pm. Then it comes out — in the car, at dinner, at bedtime — as tears, stomach aches, clinging, or a fury about the wrong cup.

Parents in Mougins, Valbonne and Antibes describe this to me every September. It's not a problem with the child. It's a small nervous system on alert for seven hours, discharging the moment it's safe. A short Reiki session at bedtime is one of the gentler ways to help that discharge happen without the fury — and it always sits alongside the paediatrician, never in place of one.

## What adjustment stress looks like

- Fine at school, falls apart at home
- Stomach aches with no cause the doctor can find
- Bedtime taking two hours; waking in the night
- Clinginess in a child who wasn't clingy
- Big reactions to small things — the sock, the cup, the wrong spoon
- Regression: a five-year-old acting three

Teachers often say the child is "doing brilliantly." They are. That's the cost.

## What a session is, for a child

Fifteen to twenty-five minutes, at bedtime, in their bed, with you in the room. The child doesn't have to lie still, close their eyes, or do anything. A book, a toy, a screen if that's what settles them. I sit beside them and rest my hands lightly on the shoulders, upper back, or feet, and keep them there. I don't talk about feelings unless they do. I don't use the word "energy." To them it's a quiet quarter of an hour with someone calm.

Most children go quiet within minutes. A lot of them fall asleep. That's the session.

## What one family saw

A child who'd been waking most nights for months after a move began, after a few bedtime sessions, to sleep through. The parent's message was one line: he'd slept the night. I don't know precisely what changed. I know a body that had been on alert had a few experiences of someone steady beside it with nothing asked, and I know a household where the child sleeps is a different household within a week.

## The parent

I'll say it every time: the most useful session in a stressed household is often the parent's. Children read the adult's nervous system before they read anything else. A settled parent at 6 pm does more than anything I can do in fifteen minutes. If you're empty, start there.

## When to see the paediatrician

Stomach pain that persists, fever, real sleep disorders, anxiety that's stopping school or eating, anything that worries you. Doctor first. I'll ask about this before we book. Reiki is complementary — the calm around the care, not the care.

## What I say to the child

Almost nothing, and that's deliberate. Children are asked to explain themselves all day at a new school. The session is a place where nobody asks. I introduce myself, ask what they're reading or watching, sit down beside them, and put my hands on their shoulders as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world — because to them, if I treat it that way, it is. The parent stays in the room. If the child wants to chat, we chat. If they go quiet, that's the session working.

## FAQ

**How can I help my child adjust to a new school abroad?**
Expect the fallout at home, not at school — it means they're coping there. Keep bedtime steady, lower demands after 4 pm, and if it's not settling, a short calm-presence session at bedtime can help a stressed small nervous system stand down.

**Is Reiki suitable for children?**
Yes, in a short form — fifteen to twenty-five minutes, parent present, nothing applied. Always alongside the paediatrician.

**How long until a child settles into a new school?**
Usually a term. If the after-school fallout is still severe after two or three months, or there are physical symptoms, see the paediatrician.

## If September is hard in your house

Message me on WhatsApp with your child's age and what bedtime looks like. Children's sessions are short and priced accordingly. If the honest answer is that you need one first, I'll say so.

## What I won't do

Treat a child instead of a paediatrician. Suggest sessions for everyone when one person needs them. Sell a family package before a first session. Reiki is complementary in every case — it works alongside medical care for the adults and the paediatrician for the children, and if I hear something that needs a doctor, I'll say so first.

## Where to start

One session for the parent who holds the most. Then we talk. The Renewal — four sessions over a month — is the shape I usually suggest for that parent, and if a child's session makes sense after that, we add it. Villas in Mougins, Valbonne, Cap d'Antibes, Biot; apartments in Cannes and Nice. I come to the house.

## The first month here

If you've just arrived — boxes still in the garage, school started last week — this is the window where a household's nervous system sets its default for the year. A session for the parent in the first month, and a bedtime one for the child if bedtime is hard, does more now than it will in March. I say this not to sell urgency but because I watch it every September in Mougins and Valbonne: the families who rest early settle faster.

## FAQ

**How does Reiki work for a family?**
As a household: the parent who holds the most goes first, because children read the adult nervous system. Sessions at home — 45 minutes for adults, fifteen to twenty-five for children at bedtime.

**Can children and parents have sessions on the same day?**
Yes, and it works well. Parent in the afternoon, child at bedtime, the house gets a steady presence for two hours.

**Is energy healing safe for expat children?**
Sessions are light hand contact with a parent present, nothing applied. Always alongside the paediatrician, never instead.

## If your house is running on empty

title: Reiki After COVID or Flu: The Fatigue That Lingers
meta_title: Reiki After COVID or Flu: The Fatigue That Lingers
meta_description: Reiki after COVID or flu — the fatigue that lingers after the infection, what people report from sessions, and where it sits alongside your doctor.
body:
The infection ends and the tiredness doesn't. Three weeks after COVID or a bad flu you're back at work, technically recovered, and hollow — flat by 3 pm, foggy, sleeping ten hours and waking unrested, a body that feels like it's running on half a battery. Doctors call it post-viral fatigue. People I see in Cannes call it "I'm not myself yet."

Reiki doesn't treat post-viral fatigue; nothing external does, and the honest answer from medicine is that it resolves with time and rest. What sessions do is make the rest real. Post-viral bodies often can't rest properly — the nervous system has been through an illness and is still on alert — and a session gets it to stand down long enough for the repair to happen.

## What post-viral fatigue actually is

An illness is a threat, and the body treats it like one. The alert system runs high throughout, and it doesn't always come down when the virus is gone. So you're left with a body that's no longer sick but still braced — poor sleep, a heart that races on the stairs, brain fog, exhaustion out of proportion to what you did. The repair the body needs happens in the parasympathetic state, and that state is exactly what a braced system can't enter.

## What sessions do

Forty-five minutes, lying down, fully clothed, at your home — post-viral bodies shouldn't be travelling anyway. Hands resting lightly on the body. Nothing asked. Most people are asleep within minutes; post-viral fatigue makes that easy. What people describe afterwards is sleep that night that finally feels like sleep, and a day after that has a little more in it.

Mandana, a client, wrote to me after a session that she hadn't felt so active since she got sick. Her words: it felt like her energy had been restored. I don't claim to have restored anything. I think her body finally had an hour where it could stop bracing and start repairing, and the difference showed the next day.

## Pacing, honestly

The mistake nearly everyone makes with post-viral fatigue is doing too much on a good day and paying for it for three. Sessions help with this in an unexpected way: an hour of enforced stillness once a week is an hour you can't overdo. Four over a month — The Renewal — gives the body four guaranteed rests, at a time when it's hard to make yourself take them.

## Where the doctor is

If fatigue is severe, lasting beyond two or three months, or comes with breathlessness, chest pain, or a racing heart at rest — doctor. Post-viral conditions sometimes need medical management, and I'm not it. Sessions sit alongside whatever your doctor does, for the rest and the settling. That's the right order and I'll say so before we book.

## What people tell me in the second week

The first session is usually sleep — most post-viral bodies fall asleep on the table within minutes and stay there. The second, a week later, is where people start to notice the daytime. "I made it to 5 pm before the wall." "I walked to the boulangerie and didn't need to sit down." Small, honest markers. I'd rather you tracked those than waited for a dramatic morning; post-viral recovery is a slope, not a switch, and the slope steepens when the body is resting properly between efforts.

## FAQ

**Can Reiki help with fatigue after COVID or flu?**
It helps a body that's still braced after an illness to rest properly, which is what post-viral recovery needs. One client said she hadn't felt so active since she got sick. It's complementary — alongside your doctor, never instead.

**How long does post-viral fatigue last?**
Usually a few weeks; sometimes two or three months. If it's severe or lasting longer, see a doctor.

**Should I have Reiki at home when recovering from illness?**
Yes. Post-viral bodies shouldn't be travelling. I come to you; you lie down; you don't have to do anything.

## If you're recovered but not yourself

Message me on WhatsApp. One session, €180, or four over a month, €640, at your home. If anything you describe needs a doctor first, I'll tell you.

title: Reiki After Surgery: Supporting Recovery (Alongside Your Doctor)
meta_title: Reiki After Surgery: Recovery Alongside Your Doctor
meta_description: Reiki after surgery — how sessions support the rest a recovering body needs, what people report about tension and sleep, and the doctor-first rule.
body:
Reiki after surgery does one thing: it helps a body that's been through a shock to rest properly while the surgeon's work does the actual healing. It doesn't speed up tissue repair, doesn't replace medication, doesn't touch the wound. What it does is get a nervous system that's been in alert — anaesthetic, pain, hospital, fear — to stand down for 45 minutes so the sleep and stillness recovery needs can happen. That's the whole claim, and it's the one I'll stand behind.

Everything that follows is under one rule: your surgeon and your doctor come first. Sessions are complementary — they sit alongside their care, never in place of it. If you're reading this before an operation, ask your surgical team whether relaxation sessions are fine during recovery. Most will say yes.

## What surgery does to the nervous system

An operation is a threat, however planned. The body braces before it, goes through it, and comes out braced — pain, disrupted sleep, the strangeness of hospital, the fear of moving wrong. Recovery is supposed to happen in the parasympathetic state, the rest-and-repair setting. A body that's still braced can't fully enter it. So people recover, but slowly and exhausted, sleeping badly and holding themselves stiff for weeks.

## What a session is, after surgery

Forty-five minutes at your home — you shouldn't be travelling. You lie however is comfortable; on your back if you can, on your side if you can't, propped up if that's what the surgeon said. Fully clothed. Hands rest lightly on the body, and I stay well away from the surgical site unless you and your doctor are fine with light contact near it. No pressure, nothing applied. Nothing asked.

What people describe is the whole body letting go of a hold it's been keeping since the operation — the shoulders, the stomach, the breath — and then sleep, often for the first time properly since the hospital.

## Pain

I won't say Reiki reduces pain. What people report is that the tension around the pain eases — the muscles that clench against it, the bracing that makes every movement hurt more than it should. When that bracing lets go, the pain often feels smaller and more contained. One client after a procedure said the session was the first time in a week she hadn't been holding her breath. Keep taking what the doctor prescribed; this sits beside it.

## Timing

Not in the first days, when the body needs undisturbed rest and the medical team's attention. From about a week after, when you're home, stable, and starting the long part of recovery. Then weekly for a month, if it helps — four sessions, The Renewal, is a natural shape for the recovery month. I'll ask what the surgeon has said before we book anything.

## What I'll ask

What the operation was. What the surgeon has said about rest, movement and touch. What you're taking. Whether there are restrictions on position. I'm not being nosy; I'm making sure the session fits the recovery rather than interferes with it. If any answer suggests a doctor should be consulted first, I'll say so.

## Two things I've seen help

First, a session the day before you're due to start moving more — the physio's next stage, the first walk further than the garden. A body that's rested and unbraced moves better and hurts less doing it. Second, a session after a difficult appointment or a hard night; recovery has bad days, and a session on one of them gives the body somewhere to put the bracing down before it becomes the new default.

## FAQ

**Can I have Reiki after surgery?**
Yes, once you're home and stable — usually from about a week after. Ask your surgical team; most are fine with relaxation sessions. I stay away from the surgical site and adjust position to whatever you've been told.

**Does Reiki help with recovery after an operation?**
It helps a braced body rest properly, which is what recovery needs. People report better sleep and less tension around the pain. It doesn't speed tissue healing or replace medication.

**Can Reiki reduce pain after surgery?**
It eases the muscular bracing around pain, which often makes the pain feel smaller. It isn't pain relief and doesn't replace what your doctor prescribed.

## If you're recovering

Message me on WhatsApp and tell me what the operation was and what your surgeon has said. One session, €180, at your home. If it isn't the right time yet, I'll tell you when it is.

title: The Three Reiki Symbols of the Second Degree — What They're For
meta_title: The Three Reiki Symbols of the Second Degree
meta_description: The three Reiki symbols of the second degree — Cho Ku Rei, Sei He Ki, Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen — what each is for, without mystification.
body:
The second degree of Usui Reiki introduces three symbols. Cho Ku Rei is used for focus and strengthening — to concentrate the work at a place or a moment. Sei He Ki is for the emotional and mental layer — used when what's being held is a feeling or a pattern rather than a physical tension. Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen is the distance symbol — it makes sessions across space and time possible, and it's why I can give a full session from Cannes to someone in London.

That's what they're for. I'm going to explain each properly, because "reiki symbols" is a much-searched phrase and most of what you'll find is either secretive or mystical, and neither is useful to someone deciding whether to book.

## A word on secrecy

Traditionally the symbols were shown only at the second-degree attunement and not drawn in public. Some lineages still hold that. Others — including many Western teachers since the 1990s — teach that the symbols are tools, not secrets, and that the attunement is what activates them for a practitioner, not the drawing. I'm in the second camp. You can see the shapes anywhere; what you can't get from a picture is the training and the transmission behind them. So I'll describe them without drama.

## Cho Ku Rei — the focus symbol

A spiral with a vertical stroke and a small flag at the top. In practice, it's the one I use most. Drawn or held in mind at the start of a session, or at a specific point on the body, it concentrates the work there — the way you'd lean in to listen more carefully. When someone's shoulders are the thing, or the jaw, Cho Ku Rei is how I stay with it.

The name is often translated as "place the power here." That's about right. It's a marker: here, now, this.

## Sei He Ki — the emotional symbol

A wave-like curve with small loops. This is the one for what isn't physical — the grief in the chest, the anxiety that has no object, the pattern someone's been running for years. In a session for someone who's braced against a feeling rather than a strain, Sei He Ki is what I bring to the chest and the head.

I don't ask people what they're feeling. The symbol is a way of working with the emotional layer without making anyone talk about it.

## Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen — the distance symbol

The most complex of the three, drawn as a column of characters — it's built from Japanese kanji and reads roughly as "no past, no present, no future" or "the origin of all is pure consciousness," depending on who's translating. What it does in practice is straightforward: it's the symbol that makes a session possible when the person isn't in the room.

This is why distance Reiki is not an internet-era invention. Second-degree practitioners have worked at a distance since the 1920s, using this symbol. When I give a session to someone in London, Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen is the first thing I use.

## What the symbols aren't

Magic. Passwords. Things that work without the training. A practitioner who's been attuned at second degree and has practised for years uses them as a musician uses scales — as structure the hands know. Someone who's found them on the internet has a drawing.

## What this means for you

If you're booking a session, the symbols mean I'm working in a defined tradition with defined tools, and that I trained for them — Level II, within a documented lineage back to Usui. If you're booking a distance session, the third symbol is the reason it exists at all. Beyond that, you don't need to think about them. They're my work, not yours. And whatever the symbols do, Reiki stays complementary — alongside medical care, never instead.

## FAQ

**What are the three Reiki symbols?**
Cho Ku Rei, for focus; Sei He Ki, for the emotional and mental layer; and Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen, the distance symbol that makes sessions across space possible. All three are taught at second degree.

**Are Reiki symbols secret?**
Traditionally yes; many Western teachers now treat them as tools rather than secrets. The shapes can be seen anywhere. What can't be copied is the attunement and training behind them.

**Which Reiki symbol is used for distance healing?**
Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen. It's why second-degree practitioners have worked at a distance since the 1920s, long before anyone did it online.

## If you'd like a session — here or at a distance

Message me on WhatsApp. In person on the Riviera or at a distance from Cannes, €180 either way. The symbols are my side of it; yours is lying down.

title: Reiki Level 1 vs Level 2: What Changes, and Why It Matters for You
meta_title: Reiki Level 1 vs Level 2: What Changes for You
meta_description: Reiki Level 1 vs Level 2 — what each degree teaches, why Level 2 makes distance sessions possible, and what to ask a practitioner about training.
body:
Reiki Level 1 teaches hands-on practice — self-treatment and treating others in person, with a set sequence of hand positions. Level 2 adds the three symbols, which bring focus, emotional work and, critically, distance practice. Level 3, or Master, is the teaching degree — the ability to attune others. If you're choosing a practitioner, Level 2 is the point at which they can give you a full session anywhere, and the point at which the practice has structure beyond the hands.

I hold Level 2, trained within a documented lineage back to Usui. Here's what that means, what it doesn't, and what to ask anyone you're considering.

## Level 1 — the hands

First degree is about the body. The student is attuned — a short ceremony that, in the tradition, opens the practitioner to the practice — and learns the hand positions: head, throat, chest, abdomen, hips, legs, feet, in sequence. They learn to treat themselves daily and to treat others in person.

Many people take Level 1 for themselves and never practise on anyone else. It's a complete thing on its own. A Level 1 practitioner can give you a good session in the room with you.

## Level 2 — the symbols

Second degree adds the three symbols and the practice that goes with them. Cho Ku Rei for focus, Sei He Ki for the emotional and mental layer, Hon Sha Ze Sho Nen for distance. There's a piece on what each is for if you want the detail.

What this changes for a client:

- **Distance sessions become possible.** A Level 1 practitioner can't give you a session when you're in London. A Level 2 practitioner can.
- **The work has more structure.** The symbols give the practitioner tools for what isn't physical — grief, anxiety, patterns — without anyone having to talk about it.
- **It's a commitment.** Level 2 usually comes after months of Level 1 practice. It's the point where someone has decided this is a discipline, not a course they did once.

## Level 3 — the teacher

Master level is about attuning others. It's the teaching degree. A Reiki Master can run Level 1 and 2 courses. It doesn't, in itself, make someone a better practitioner — some of the best hands-on practitioners I know stopped at Level 2, and some Masters teach far more than they treat.

## What to ask a practitioner

- **What level?** Level 2 is what you want for full sessions and distance.
- **Who trained you, in what lineage?** A named teacher and a line back to Usui. I show mine; I'd be wary of anyone who won't.
- **How long have you practised?** Level matters less than years of hands on bodies.
- **Will you tell me to see a doctor?** The right answer is "yes, when you should." Reiki is complementary — alongside medical care, not instead — and a practitioner who won't say so hasn't understood the practice.

## My training

Level 1 in December 2025 and Level 2 in February 2026, both in Usui Reiki Ryoho within a documented lineage — Usui, Hayashi, Takata, and forward to my teacher. Both diplomas are on the homepage. I mention this not because certificates are the point but because you should be able to check.

## What each level feels like to receive

Honestly, in the room, a good Level 1 session and a good Level 2 session feel much the same — hands, warmth, the drop. The difference shows in what the practitioner can do when the thing you're carrying isn't physical, and in whether they can give you a session when you're in another country. If you're only ever going to be on the table in front of them, Level 1 is enough. If your life moves, Level 2 is the one that moves with it.

## FAQ

**What's the difference between Reiki Level 1 and Level 2?**
Level 1 is hands-on practice in person. Level 2 adds the three symbols — focus, emotional work, and distance — and is the degree at which full sessions can be given anywhere.

**Do I need a Level 2 practitioner?**
For in-person sessions, a good Level 1 practitioner is fine. For distance sessions, Level 2 is required — it's what makes them possible.

**Is a Reiki Master better than Level 2?**
Not necessarily. Master is the teaching degree. Years of hands-on practice matter more than the title.

## If you'd like to see the training before you book

Both diplomas are on the homepage, with the lineage. Message me on WhatsApp with any question about them — I'd rather you asked than wondered.

title: Usui Reiki Lineage: Why I Show You My Teacher's Name
meta_title: Usui Reiki Lineage: Why I Show My Teacher's Name
meta_description: What a Usui Reiki lineage is, why it matters when choosing a practitioner abroad, and the line from Usui to my teacher — shown, not hinted at.
body:
A Reiki lineage is the chain of teachers from Mikao Usui, who founded the practice in Japan in the 1920s, to the person whose hands are on you. Usui taught Chujiro Hayashi; Hayashi taught Hawayo Takata; Takata brought Reiki to the West and taught the twenty-two Masters from whom nearly every Western practitioner descends. From there the line branches, and each practitioner's lineage is the specific branch that reaches them.

Mine runs from Usui through Hayashi and Takata, forward through a line of Ukrainian and European teachers, to Olena Yushko, who attuned me at Levels 1 and 2. Her name is on my diplomas and the diplomas are on my homepage. I show this because it's the one thing about a Reiki practitioner you can actually verify, and because a practitioner who won't show it is asking you to take more on faith than I think is fair.

## Why lineage matters

In most traditions that pass something by hand — music, craft, martial arts — you can ask who taught your teacher and trace the line. Reiki is the same. The attunement — the short transmission at each degree — is what makes someone a practitioner rather than someone who's read a book, and it can only be received from someone who received it. No line, no attunement. No attunement, no practice.

This doesn't mean a longer lineage is better, or that one branch outranks another. It means the line exists and is documented. That's the check.

## What a real lineage looks like

Names. Dates. A teacher you can find. Mine, as written on the diploma:

Usui → Hayashi → Takata → (through Furumoto, and a line of European and Ukrainian Masters) → Olena Yushko → me.

Yushko is a Reiki Master-Teacher in Ukraine who has trained practitioners for many years in the Usui system. My Level 1 was December 2025, Level 2 February 2026. That's recent, and I'd rather say so than imply otherwise — what I bring alongside it is a family line of healers, ten years of sitting with people in corporate rooms, and a practice I do daily.

## What a lineage doesn't tell you

Whether the practitioner is any good. Whether they'll be on time. Whether they'll tell you to see a doctor when you should. Lineage is the floor, not the ceiling. It tells you the practice is real; it doesn't tell you the person is right for you. That, you find out in a session.

## Why this matters more abroad

If you're choosing a practitioner in your own country, in your own language, you have context — reviews you can read, friends who know someone. On the Riviera, in English, you mostly have the practitioner's word. Lineage is the piece of their word you can check. Ask for it. Ask everyone for it. The ones who show it without being asked are usually the ones to trust.

## The Ukrainian branch

People sometimes ask why a practitioner in Cannes trained through Ukraine. Because that's where I'm from, where my grandfather practised long before the word Reiki reached him, and where I found a teacher I trusted. The Usui system is the same everywhere; the branch is where the teacher happens to be. Reiki spread through the Soviet space in the 1990s through exactly the same Takata line as everywhere else.

Reiki is complementary — alongside medical care, never instead. That's true in every lineage, and any practitioner in any line who tells you otherwise has stepped outside it.

## What I'd ask of any lineage claim

Three things. Is the teacher named — a real person you could find? Is the line back to Usui written down, not just implied? And does the practitioner say, without being pushed, what they *don't* have — a Master level, decades of practice, a French qualification? The ones who volunteer their limits are usually the ones whose claims are true. Lineage is a chain of people telling the truth about who taught them. It only works if the last link does too.

## FAQ

**What is a Reiki lineage?**
The chain of teachers from Mikao Usui to your practitioner — Usui, Hayashi, Takata, and the branch from there. It documents that the attunements were received, which is what makes the practice real.

**How do I check a Reiki practitioner's lineage?**
Ask for the teacher's name and the line back to Usui. Diplomas should show it. Mine are on my homepage with Olena Yushko named as teacher.

**Does a longer lineage mean a better practitioner?**
No. Lineage confirms the practice is genuine. Skill comes from years of hands on bodies, and that you find out in a session.

## If you'd like to see it

Both diplomas, with the lineage, are on the homepage. Message me on WhatsApp if you want to know more about the line — I'll tell you what I know and what I don't.

title: Reiki Before an Important Meeting or Decision
meta_title: Reiki Before an Important Meeting or Decision
meta_description: Reiki before an important meeting or decision — one session the evening before, what changes in the room, and what a client stuck on a choice found.
body:
The evening before a decision that matters, most people do one of two things: work on it more, or try to distract themselves from it. Both keep the nervous system in alert, and alert is the worst state to decide anything in — it narrows attention, favours the defensive option, and makes every choice feel like a threat. A Reiki session the evening before does the opposite: it gets the body to stand down, and a body that has stood down thinks differently in the morning.

This is one of the more practical things I do in Cannes — for founders before a board, for people before a negotiation, for anyone before a conversation they've been dreading. Here's what it is and what it isn't.

## What alert does to a decision

In alert, the mind runs on threat logic: what could go wrong, what to defend, what to avoid. It's fast and it's narrow. Good for a genuine emergency; bad for anything that needs perspective. People walk into meetings braced and make the choice that felt safest at 2 am, which is rarely the best one.

The body can't be talked out of alert. It has to be given evidence that it's safe — stillness, warmth, nothing needed — long enough to believe it. That's what a session is.

## The evening-before session

Forty-five minutes, at your home or my space in Cannes, ideally between 6 and 9 pm. You lie down, fully clothed. Hands rest lightly on the body. No conversation about the meeting — I don't want to know, and you don't need to rehearse. Most people drop into deep rest around minute ten and come up with the thing they've been circling suddenly looking smaller and clearer.

Sleep that night is usually good. That alone changes the room.

## What people notice in the meeting

"I wasn't braced." "I noticed I could hear what they were actually saying." "I said the thing I'd been avoiding and it was fine." A founder I work with put it as: the difference between arriving as the person who's been up since five and arriving as himself.

I don't claim the session makes the decision. It makes the person who's deciding available.

## When it's a decision, not a meeting

One client came to me stuck on a hard choice about a relationship — not to talk about it; she'd talked about it for months. She wanted to stop going in circles. After the session she said something had settled and she knew what to do next, which was not the dramatic option she'd been rehearsing. I don't take credit for the answer. I think it was there and the noise was in the way.

## What it won't do

Give you the answer. Replace preparation. Turn a bad plan into a good one. And if the sleeplessness before decisions has become a pattern, or the anxiety before meetings is disabling, that's worth a doctor's attention — Reiki is complementary, alongside that care, not instead.

## The morning of

If the evening before isn't possible, the morning works — two or three hours before the meeting, not immediately before. You want time to come up from the session, drink water, and arrive with the calm settled rather than fresh. A session at 8 for an 11 o'clock board is right. A session at 10 for the same board leaves you pleasantly vague at exactly the wrong moment.

## FAQ

**Can Reiki help before an important meeting?**
It gets the nervous system out of alert the evening before, so you sleep and walk in as yourself rather than braced. People describe hearing the room better and saying what they'd been avoiding.

**When should I have a session before a big decision?**
The evening before, between 6 and 9 pm. Sleep does the rest. The morning of is second best.

**Does Reiki help with decision-making?**
It doesn't make the decision; it clears the alert state that narrows thinking. One client stuck for months on a choice said something settled after a session and she knew her next step.

## If tomorrow matters

Message me on WhatsApp today. One session, €180, this evening at your home or my space in Cannes. Same-day slots are often possible, and this is exactly what they're for.

title: Wellness on Holiday in Cannes: A Week That Actually Restores Something
meta_title: Wellness Holiday in Cannes: A Week That Restores
meta_description: Wellness on holiday in Cannes — why most weeks don't restore anything, and a rhythm of three Reiki sessions that makes one that does.
body:
Most holidays on the Riviera don't restore anything. People arrive braced from the flight, spend the first three days adjusting, have two good ones, and then start thinking about going back. They return home with a tan and the same nervous system they left with. The holiday changed the scenery; it didn't change the state.

A week that actually restores something needs a rhythm — not a spa schedule, not a programme, just three moments where the body is given a real chance to stand down. I've built one for people staying in Cannes and along the coast. It's called Your Week Here, and here's the logic.

## Why the first three days are lost

A long flight puts the nervous system in alert: noise, dry air, no sleep, a body held still for hours. You land at Nice, drive forty minutes to a hotel on the Croisette, and you're horizontal by the pool by 4 pm — with a heart rate that hasn't got the message. Sleep that night is broken. Day two you're tired and wired. Day three you're starting to arrive. That's most of a week's holiday gone to adjustment.

## Session one: arrival

Within 48 hours of landing. In your hotel room or villa, 45 minutes, fully clothed. The body gets a strong signal that it's safe to stand down, and most people sleep properly that night. The adjustment that would have taken three days takes one. There's a longer piece on [how to deal with jet lag after travel](/journal/how-to-deal-with-jet-lag-after-travel/) if you want the detail; this is the practical version of it.

## Session two: midway

Around day four or five. By now the holiday has started — you've had a good dinner, a day on the water at Îles de Lérins, a morning that began without an alarm. This is the session that takes it deeper. The body is already partly down; a session here goes further than the first, and people describe the second half of the week as different in kind, not just degree.

## Session three: before you leave

The day before you fly. The week has been good and you'd like it to settle before it ends — to arrive home with the state, not just the memory. A session the last evening does that. People tell me the flight home was the calmest they'd had, and that the first week back didn't erase everything the way it usually does.

## What it isn't

A retreat. A programme. Something you have to show up to at set times. Each session is 45 minutes at your accommodation at a time that suits — I fit around your week, not the other way round. There's no yoga, no diet, no journal. Just three hours across a week where nothing is asked of you.

## Who it's for

Couples and families on a week's stay. Solo travellers who came here specifically to stop. People on a charter. Anyone who's had too many holidays that didn't work.

## The honest limit

If you're here for three days, one session — the Arrival Reset — is the right shape. If you're here for a month, we talk about something longer. And if you're unwell, that's a doctor's conversation first; Reiki is complementary, and a holiday is not a substitute for care.

## What it costs and what it replaces

Your Week Here is €480 for three sessions — the same per-session rate as the four-session package, for a week rather than a month. It replaces, in most people's weeks, the three afternoons that would otherwise have gone to lying by the pool not quite resting. Nothing else about the holiday changes. You still eat where you were going to eat and swim where you were going to swim. You just arrive at those things with a body that's actually there.

## FAQ

**How do you actually relax on holiday?**
By giving the nervous system real signals of safety early — not just scenery. One session in the first 48 hours cuts the adjustment from three days to one, and the rest of the week starts sooner.
